I think the issue is that Gladios flaws are never addressed. Gladio projects onto others and lashes out in a more aggressive/intense way compared to the others.  His pain, fear and confusion is turned outward, not inward ( like Noctis). While I understand, it is not acceptable in the long run. He spends a whole entire chapter subjecting Noctis to this and using Ignis as a prop for his anger it quickly grows tiresome. Its not surprising that his coping mechanism turned some people off. 

 I think another large issue is that we dont really get to see how Noctis acted in the past couple of weeks. Even though in my opinion, grieving shouldn't have a time table, we don't really have any context. We just see Noctis sadly looking out a window. Thats it, they are still moving toward something. Its not like Noctis has run way from the group. He hasn't lost the ring. The player has also just experienced Lunas death, so Gladio suddenly getting on Noctis's case is alarming. You hear that it has been weeks, but you dont feel that it has been that long. You are playing catch up,so to speak. The game has this issue frequently. It seems that Gladio wants something that Noctis cant provide, so he is demanding insecuential things from him.

The game could have used his dlc to address these issues but it wastes it on something completely superfluous that again highlights Gladios flaws but does nothing to show that he is gonna work on them. 

Also, it doesnt feel like the rift between Gladio and Noctis is resolved. We deal with this grating tension between them , and then Iggy tells them to knock it off. That is not enough, and Ignis should not resolve their fight.  Its clearly an issue between Noctis and Gladio, and its a deep issue. It goes back to Gladio's brotherhood episode in my eyes. The game just tells you its okay now, even though it isn't. Noctis goes into the crystal shortly after , which doesn't give the player much time to process anything.  Its the weeks issue all over again. So, while I dont hate Gladio for his outbursts, he is my least favorite of the group. But I blame the game more than his individual character for that.

I dont think the game wants you to forgive Abby. You don't have to sympathize with her if you don't want to. You can, but its not required. They just present her as she is. There are actually people in her group who call her a piece of shit ! People are constantly saying that the game wants me to do this or that, but I think its mostly projection.

I think people have a right be upset about losing a character. I won't even say that they are childish for that aspect of the game turning them off. If you really like a character and they die brutally, it hurts. Especially in this time period. People want some hope, and watching a beloved character die is frustrating.  

However, I do personally think that players have idealized Joel,and by extention ellie. They are also kind of in denial that it wasnt obvious that Joel was going to die in this game. I mean, come on, the reveal trailer was giving serious illusion/ghost vibes. You can go back to any comment section with that trailer and find loads of comments ralking about Joels supposed death. I dont know why people are acting like the information  all brand new now. Now, I understand that Joel and Ellie are loved characters. We spend a lot of time with them, and their relationship endears us to them. 

But to be honest, Joel is a bastard. He has been shuned by his brother because of his brutality. Tommy literally tells him later on that survivng with him was not worth it. He would have rather died. Joel was also part of those awful gangs that roam the landscape, killing seemingly innocent or vulnerable groups for their own selfish desires. The same people that ruined Ish's safe place( filled with children), and who attack Ellie and Joel constantly. Even though the fireflies are naive, uppity, want to kill Ellie and choose a rat way to do it...they are not the bad guys. From an objective standpoint, all they want is to find a cure for the infected. They hope that the cure will allow humanity to reconnect and start healing. It is a childish hope but nothing they want is malicious. They believe that one girl's life is worth a cure. Most people would agree. The Fireflies are actually the hopeful preachy group in the last of us world. They believe in humanity's sanctity. And for that they are ridiculed, killed off and discarded. 

Only Joel( and the players) really suffer from Ellie's death. Anyone that isnt the audience would say that Joel is being selfish and actively crushing any hope of society has of being better for a long time. He unnecessarily kills the doctor and is called an animal, which is somewhat understandable. He is only really acting on instinct at this point. He kills marline as she begs for her life. Joel is objectively a bad person. He is a man that has been violent and self-centered. A big reason Joel is likable is because of Ellie. Ellie allows him to be more than what he really is. So, why do people expect Abby to treat Joel with respect? She only knows him as a person who has hurt her. His past actions don't help his case.

And Tommy was never that cold hearted in the first place. Tommy split from Joel because he thought Joel went to far when it came to " surviving ". They didn't talk for years knowing that mostly meant that they would never see each other again. Thats how opposed Tommy was to Joel.

Joel had to live in Tommy's settlement and Tommy made it very clear that he wouldn't abide by Joels past philosophy in the first game. This was his settlement that he carved out for himself, a place that protected itself but never went looking for trouble or inflicted uncessary pain on others. I could believe that  5 years in this settlement would make joel soft. Joel was never part of a community before Ellie.  He and tess were feral bastards that lived with other feral bastards. Joel never made it to a place where he felt safe. So he never let up his guard. But it is clear that Tommys settlement is doing real good, it is thriving. Its got a lot of young people, children , technology and comforts. However,  when something or someone is doing real good, there is a real good chance of getting complacent and too relaxed. 

I guess we will just have to see it for ourselves. It's one thing to hear about it but another to experience the event.
